concept.premise: In an early-1990s local TV station being squeezed by cable, consolidation, and the first rumblings of the internet, late-night horror host Madame Massacre fights to stay relevant while a media conglomerate’s takeover reveals a literal demonic agenda. As the station’s on-air camp and off-air reality blur in a world where the macabre is treated as merely eccentric, Maddie must use her wit, sex appeal, and horror-host savvy to outplay infernal corporate power.
concept.tone: Satirical, bawdy, adult, and campy; sharp workplace/media satire with occult horror used primarily as a vehicle for comedy.
concept.setting: A local television station in the early 1990s, during a period of industry upheaval from cable expansion, early internet culture, and media consolidation. The story world treats gothic and supernatural oddities with an Addams Family-like casualness rather than awe.
concept.protagonist: Madame Massacre ("Maddie"), the player character: a sexy late-night horror host in the tradition of Vampira, Elvira, and Lily Munster. She is the same persona on-screen and off-screen—confident, seductive, and razor-witted, but privately anxious that she is becoming obsolete as both a performer and cultural figure.
concept.core_hook: A predatory media conglomerate moves to absorb Maddie’s struggling station, led by a polished executive who is quite literally a demon from hell. To save her station, her show, and her own sense of relevance, Madame Massacre must navigate corporate corruption, occult peril, and the ridiculous dysfunction of local television.
must_have_elements: Madame Massacre as the direct player-character POV
An early-1990s local TV station under pressure from cable, the nascent internet, and media consolidation
Campy occult horror with real supernatural peril, but treated with casual normalcy within the world
A demonic corporate suit/executive spearheading the station takeover
The station news team’s sports anchor as a major character: a grown-up high-school-jock type
An open-secret, on-and-off sexual relationship between Maddie and the sports anchor
Adult Swim-style bawdy adult humor and satire
concept.concept_summary: Set inside a shabby early-1990s local TV station, this horror-comedy follows Madame Massacre, a seductive late-night horror host who realizes she may be aging into obsolescence just as her employer faces corporate annihilation. The buyer is a hellish media conglomerate fronted by an actual demon in a suit, turning industry consolidation into both a satirical and supernatural threat. In a world where gothic weirdness is treated as normal background texture, Maddie must weaponize her charisma, wit, and horror-host theatrics to survive occult corporate warfare, station dysfunction, and her messy on-and-off affair with the station’s jockish sports anchor.

narrative_design_spec.story_title: Madame Massacre vs. the Merger from Hell
narrative_design_spec.synopsis: In a shabby early-1990s local TV station battered by cable expansion, media consolidation, and the first awkward chirps of internet culture, late-night horror host Madame Massacre fights to keep her show, her station, and her own relevance alive. The world treats gothic oddities and real occult phenomena with breezy normalcy, which becomes a problem when polished executive Lucien Vale arrives to acquire the station on behalf of Acheron Media Group and turns out to be a literal demon in a power suit. Through direct player-character POV as Maddie, the story blends bawdy comedy, workplace satire, and camp supernatural peril as she weaponizes charisma, wit, and horror-host showmanship alongside her on-and-off lover Rex, a jockish sports anchor, and a dysfunctional station staff to stop an infernal corporate takeover.

character_data.name: Madame Massacre
character_data.portrait_image_prompt: A glamorous early-1990s horror hostess with pale skin, towering black beehive hair, dramatic arched brows, smoky eye makeup, sharp cheekbones, crimson lips, long black nails, a voluptuous figure, a plunging black gown with cobweb lace, silver occult jewelry, and a confident seductive smile.
dialogue_examples: Darling, if this station cuts my budget any further, I'll have to start sacrificing union extras.
I've built a career on making the grotesque look inviting. Corporate management is the first monster to return the favor.
If Rex stops by my dressing room after sports, that's between me, him, and several offended pieces of furniture.
Obsolete? Please. Camp never dies; it just gets pushed to a later time slot.

character_data.name: Rex Rundle
character_data.portrait_image_prompt: A handsome early-30s local TV sports anchor with a broad-shouldered former-jock build, square jaw, feathered blond-brown hair, a bright smile, rolled-up dress shirt sleeves, a loud patterned tie, and easy masculine confidence.
dialogue_examples: Look, Maddie, I'm not saying the new guy's evil, but his handshake felt like a toaster in a bathtub.
I do sports, babe. If a thing has stats, shoulder pads, or both, I can fight it.
We are absolutely keeping this professional. Soon as the newsroom stops making kissy noises.
I peaked in high school, but I peaked athletically. Morally, I'm still developing.

character_data.name: Lucien Vale
character_data.portrait_image_prompt: A polished middle-aged media executive with slick dark hair, unnaturally handsome features, a predatory smile, immaculate charcoal power suit, crimson silk tie, expensive cufflinks, subtly inhuman eyes, and elegant menacing poise.
dialogue_examples: I don't destroy local culture, Madame Massacre. I monetize its afterlife.
Viewers don't want personality anymore. They want familiarity, compliance, and repeatable demographics.
A merger is simply a ritual in which the weaker body invites the stronger spirit inside.
You call it hellish. I call it vertical integration.

character_data.name: Dottie Graves
character_data.portrait_image_prompt: A hard-bitten woman in her 50s with a severe bob haircut, tired eyes, shoulder-padded businesswear, reading glasses on a chain, cigarette-holder elegance, and a no-nonsense expression with traces of dry glamour.
dialogue_examples: I've survived three owners, six formats, and a raccoon in the weather wall. A demon in a necktie doesn't impress me.
If the building catches fire, fill out the incident form before you scream.
Around here, the supernatural is only a problem when it affects ad sales.
Maddie, I don't need miracles. I need deliverables.

character_data.name: Tina "Packet" Morales
character_data.portrait_image_prompt: A sharp young Latina broadcast engineer with curly dark hair in a messy ponytail, chunky glasses, skeptical eyes, an oversized early-1990s sweater, a utility belt, grease-pencil marks on her fingers, and a clever smirk.
dialogue_examples: The station computer crashed because Blaine tried to store his headshots on the weather machine again.
I've been on bulletin boards all week. Trust me, the weirdos online think your boss is either a demon or from New Jersey.
Analog equipment is honest. It hums, overheats, and dies right in front of you.
If hell runs on proprietary software, I can absolutely ruin its evening.

character_data.name: Blaine Bixby
character_data.portrait_image_prompt: A vain middle-aged news anchor with immaculate helmet hair, a capped-teeth smile, square chin, silk pocket square, expensive grooming, and an aggressively reassuring expression radiating polished local-celebrity vanity.
dialogue_examples: People trust me, because my hair has never once admitted uncertainty.
This is not panic. This is a premium-grade concern suitable for a lead story.
I did not sell out. I aligned myself with the future while keeping my options photogenic.
If Satan wants the six o'clock hour, he can damn well wait through commercial.

location_data.name: Studio B - Madame Massacre Set
location_data.location_image_prompt: A shabby early-1990s local TV horror-host soundstage with fake stone crypt walls, foam tombstones, velvet drapes, dusty cobweb props, a coffin-shaped host desk, practical effects clutter, chunky broadcast cameras, visible cables, CRT monitors, and low-budget camp charm.

location_data.name: Newsroom and Sports Desk
location_data.location_image_prompt: A cramped early-1990s local television newsroom with beige desktop computers, ringing phones, cluttered assignment boards, coffee-stained desks, weather maps, a small sports anchor station, VHS tapes, wire baskets, fluorescent office grit, and fading station branding.

location_data.name: Executive Conference Room
location_data.location_image_prompt: An aging station boardroom with faux wood paneling, a long conference table, takeover binders, legal pads, an overhead projector, framed regional broadcasting awards, stale corporate decor, and slick new conglomerate branding awkwardly invading the room.

location_data.name: Basement Master Control and Tape Archive
location_data.location_image_prompt: A concrete basement broadcast control area packed with humming equipment racks, blinking switchboards, patch cables, tape shelves, old film canisters, transmitter schematics, maintenance notes, analog monitors, and occult sigils hidden among engineering markings.

scene_data.narrative_summary: During a taping of her late-night horror show, Maddie performs through collapsing props, shrinking budgets, and backstage rumors that the station is about to be sold. The player is introduced to the station's shabby-camp culture, Maddie's flirty chemistry with sports anchor Rex, and Dottie's dry warnings about looming corporate buyers. The scene ends when a sleek takeover promo abruptly hijacks a studio monitor and Maddie gets her first glimpse of Lucien Vale smiling like he already owns the building.

The next day in the newsroom, cable panic, ratings anxiety, and half-baked internet talk have everyone on edge as Lucien formally arrives from Acheron Media Group. Blaine fawns over him, Rex bristles, and Dottie tries to keep the station from embarrassing itself while Lucien frames the takeover as inevitable modernization. Maddie needles him in front of the staff and notices that his polished corporate jargon sounds disturbingly similar to ritual language.

At the acquisition meeting, Lucien unveils a rebrand plan that would erase local personalities in favor of sterile syndicated sameness. Maddie publicly skewers his buzzwords, buying just enough time for Tina to notice occult sigils and predatory clauses buried in the merger documents and the station charter. Dottie reluctantly grants Maddie a short window to investigate before the sale becomes final.

In the basement master control room and tape archive, Maddie teams with Tina and Rex to dig through broadcast logs, public-access oddities, and the station's bizarre founding paperwork. They discover the original transmitter accidentally functioned as a protective ward and that Acheron has been buying stations to convert regional signals into an infernal relay network. Rex also admits he saw Lucien's face slip into something horned and inhuman, turning suspicion into certainty.

Maddie turns her live show into a trap, delivering a campy anti-corporate monologue packed with innuendo, horror-host theatrics, and deliberately provocative audience bait. The stunt causes a surge of call-ins and attention that briefly disrupts Lucien's control over the station signal, proving that live local chaos can weaken his ritual power. Lucien retaliates by accelerating the takeover and threatening to replace Maddie with a sanitized, market-tested late-night host.

With the merger hours from completion, Lucien divides the staff through severance promises, vanity plays, and fear, and Blaine briefly sides with him to protect his career. Maddie rallies Rex, Tina, and Dottie by reframing the station's cheapness, intimacy, and unpredictability as strengths no corporate machine can fully control. When Blaine realizes Lucien intends to consume the station's identity rather than merely own it, he defects and reveals the timing and mechanics of the midnight merger ritual.

In the executive conference room, directly tied into the station's signal chain, Lucien begins the final merger ritual by fusing contracts, stock transfers, and live broadcast routing into a literal infernal acquisition. Tina sabotages the signal path, Dottie weaponizes procedural loopholes, Rex buys time with a mix of bravado and brawn, and Blaine creates an on-air distraction. Maddie defeats Lucien by dragging his demonic grandeur into a live spectacle so tacky and publicly humiliating that audience laughter strips him of mystique and breaks his hold on the station.

After Lucien's defeat, the station survives as a proudly strange local outlet, saved less by polish than by solidarity, shamelessness, and live unpredictability. Maddie returns to the air and turns the attempted hell-merger into sensational late-night television, reclaiming her relevance without softening her persona. Rex and Maddie's relationship remains openly messy, the staff settles into a new dysfunctional equilibrium, and the station faces the future bruised, horny, and defiantly on air.

beat_sheets.story_title: Madame Massacre vs. the Merger from Hell
beat_sheets.source_scene_summary: During a taping of her late-night horror show, Maddie performs through collapsing props, shrinking budgets, and backstage rumors that the station is about to be sold. The player is introduced to the station's shabby-camp culture, Maddie's flirty chemistry with sports anchor Rex, and Dottie's dry warnings about looming corporate buyers. The scene ends when a sleek takeover promo abruptly hijacks a studio monitor and Maddie gets her first glimpse of Lucien Vale smiling like he already owns the building.
beat_sheets.dramatic_question: Can Maddie keep her show gloriously under control through another night of low-budget chaos before the rumored sale becomes a real threat?
beat_sheets.scene_goal: Finish the taping with style, protect the value of her on-air persona, and find out whether the station-sale rumors are serious.
beat_sheets.scene_turn: What begins as familiar, manageable production chaos turns into a concrete outside threat when a polished Acheron promo hijacks the set and gives Maddie her first look at Lucien Vale.

beats.purpose: Introduce Maddie in full horror-host mode and establish the show's shabby-camp identity through a problem she must instantly perform through.
beats.summary: Maddie opens a segment of Madame Massacre's show in character as a foam tombstone lists sideways and a cheap raven effect sputters out behind her. The player chooses how she folds the malfunction into her patter, showing that Maddie's charisma turns technical failure into part of the act.
beats.revelation: The show is operating on such a thin budget that even basic props can barely survive a take.
beats.player_goal: Keep the opening segment smooth without breaking character.
beats.choice_prompt: How does Maddie cover the collapsing prop on-air?
branch_outcomes: She turns it into a sultry double entendre.
She mocks the production disaster with acid camp wit.
She leans into spooky grandeur and pretends the set is genuinely cursed.
beats.exit_state: Maddie proves she can dominate the camera even when the set literally falls apart around her.

beats.purpose: Ground the comedy in real station decline and seed the first rumors that the budget crisis is connected to a sale.
beats.summary: During a reset, Tina rushes in with tape, tools, and exhausted sarcasm to prop the scenery back into something broadcastable. While patching things together, she grumbles that engineering has been denied replacements for weeks and mentions crew gossip that management may be starving departments because buyers are circling.
beats.revelation: The station's worsening cheapness may be deliberate pre-sale neglect rather than ordinary penny-pinching.
beats.player_goal: Figure out whether tonight's chaos is just routine budget pain or a sign of something bigger.
beats.exit_state: Maddie starts to suspect the station's decay is tied to an impending ownership change.

beats.purpose: Introduce Rex's chemistry with Maddie and give the rumor a wider station context through playful banter.
beats.summary: Rex swings by the set on a flimsy excuse, brightening the room with a grin and easy jock swagger that immediately turns into flirtation. Between jokes about Maddie's collapsing crypt, he admits the newsroom is buzzing about outside suits and that the whole building feels jumpy.
beats.revelation: The sale rumor has spread beyond the set; even the newsroom believes change is coming.
beats.player_goal: Enjoy Rex's attention while gauging how seriously to take the station gossip.
beats.choice_prompt: How does Maddie handle Rex's shameless mid-taping flirtation?
branch_outcomes: She escalates the flirting and reinforces their messy chemistry.
She keeps him teasingly at arm's length and stays work-focused.
She hides her concern behind sharper jokes and a cooler facade.
beats.exit_state: Maddie and Rex's attraction is clear, and the rumor now feels like a station-wide pressure rather than backstage chatter.

beats.purpose: Bring in Dottie as the pragmatic authority figure and confirm that the sale threat is real enough to affect how everyone behaves.
beats.summary: Dottie cuts through the flirtation with a clipboard, a deadline, and the emotional warmth of an overdue memo. She dryly confirms that corporate buyers may be visiting soon and warns Maddie that eccentric, expensive local personalities are exactly the kind of assets polished management likes to erase first.
beats.revelation: The threat is official enough that Dottie is already managing the station around prospective buyers' scrutiny.
beats.player_goal: Read whether Dottie is trying to protect her, warn her, or soften her up for cuts.
beats.choice_prompt: How does Maddie answer Dottie's warning about the buyers?
branch_outcomes: She promises just enough professionalism to keep Dottie onside.
She argues that her weirdness is the station's strongest asset.
She deflects with gallows humor while refusing to sound scared.
beats.exit_state: Maddie can no longer dismiss the sale as rumor; management is bracing for real outside interference.

beats.purpose: Show Maddie's professionalism and why the station's messy local personality is worth defending before the intrusion arrives.
beats.summary: Maddie steps back into the lights and powers through another segment, turning dead fog cues, crooked scenery, and exhausted crew timing into intimate late-night charm. Tina, Rex, and even Dottie are reminded that the show's cheapness is inseparable from the live, unpredictable personality that makes it work.
beats.revelation: Maddie's ability to make chaos feel alive is a real strength, not just a coping mechanism.
beats.player_goal: Finish the taping strong and prove her show still deserves to exist.
beats.exit_state: The set regains its rhythm, making the station's oddball identity feel vivid and defensible.

beats.purpose: Deliver the inciting intrusion by transforming vague economic anxiety into a specific, embodied antagonist.
beats.summary: Without warning, a studio monitor glitches away from the expected feed and rolls a sleek corporate promo that looks alien inside Studio B's dusty gloom. The spot introduces Acheron Media and lands on Lucien Vale's immaculate, predatory smile, giving Maddie the unmistakable feeling that someone has already started taking possession of her world.
beats.revelation: Acheron Media is not a distant rumor; it has already reached into the studio, and Lucien Vale is the face of the takeover.
beats.player_goal: Understand what just hijacked the room and who Lucien Vale is.
beats.exit_state: The scene ends with Maddie's familiar production problems replaced by a concrete corporate menace she can no longer ignore.

beat_sheets.story_title: Madame Massacre vs. the Merger from Hell
beat_sheets.source_scene_summary: The next day in the newsroom, cable panic, ratings anxiety, and half-baked internet talk have everyone on edge as Lucien formally arrives from Acheron Media Group. Blaine fawns over him, Rex bristles, and Dottie tries to keep the station from embarrassing itself while Lucien frames the takeover as inevitable modernization. Maddie needles him in front of the staff and notices that his polished corporate jargon sounds disturbingly similar to ritual language.
beat_sheets.dramatic_question: Can Maddie puncture Lucien Vale's polished modernization pitch enough to learn what kind of monster has actually walked into her station?
beat_sheets.scene_goal: Size up Lucien, defend the station's personality in front of the staff, and test whether his takeover language hides something more sinister than ordinary corporate greed.
beat_sheets.scene_turn: Lucien successfully presents the takeover as inevitable to much of the staff, but Maddie's public sparring with him reveals a deeper threat: his merger rhetoric sounds uncannily like ritual language, turning her contempt into active suspicion.

beats.purpose: Establish the newsroom's anxious atmosphere and show how vulnerable the station already is to promises of rescue or modernization.
beats.summary: Maddie enters a newsroom running on burnt coffee, cable panic, ratings dread, and confused chatter about whether computer bulletin boards are somehow the future of television. Rex shares his unease, Blaine rehearses his charm for the incoming buyer, and Dottie warns everyone not to disgrace the station before the meeting even starts.
beats.revelation: The station's fear of cable expansion and emerging internet culture has made the staff unusually susceptible to anyone promising a stable future.
beats.player_goal: Read the room and identify who is panicking, posturing, or ready to fight before Lucien arrives.
beats.exit_state: Maddie realizes the station is already half-defeated by insecurity before any contract has been signed.

beats.purpose: Introduce Lucien in person and let his presence immediately shift the power dynamic in the room.
beats.summary: Dottie corrals the staff into something resembling professionalism just as Lucien Vale arrives, immaculate and unnervingly self-possessed amid the newsroom clutter. Blaine practically glows with approval, Rex stiffens on instinct, and Lucien greets people like assets he has already inventoried.
beats.revelation: Lucien already knows key staff by name, function, and perceived market value, suggesting Acheron has done more than casual due diligence.
beats.player_goal: Study Lucien up close and see how he works the room before he can define himself on his own terms.
beats.exit_state: Lucien establishes himself as charming, prepared, and subtly predatory.

beats.purpose: Lay out the corporate threat in public language and expose the first visible fractures among the staff.
beats.summary: Lucien delivers a sleek speech about fragmentation, modernization, and the necessity of unified branding in a changing media landscape. Blaine eagerly endorses the future, Rex bristles at the implied contempt for local identity, and Dottie tries to keep the whole thing from turning into open mutiny.
beats.revelation: Acheron's version of modernization means reducing local personalities into standardized, interchangeable brand pieces.
beats.player_goal: Figure out what Lucien's plans would actually mean for Madame Massacre and the rest of the station.
beats.exit_state: The conflict clarifies from vague sale anxiety into a direct threat to the station's identity.

beats.purpose: Give the player control over Maddie's first public challenge and force Lucien off his prepared script.
beats.summary: Rather than let Lucien's inevitability pitch settle over the newsroom, Maddie cuts in and challenges him in front of everyone. Whether she goes for flirtatious mockery, hometown defiance, or a deceptively polite business question, she drags the conversation back into personality and makes Lucien answer her directly.
beats.mood: playful on the surface, confrontational underneath
beats.revelation: Lucien instantly recognizes Maddie as the only person in the room willing to oppose him publicly rather than just react to him.
beats.player_goal: Test Lucien's composure, reclaim the room's attention, and see what slips when he has to improvise.
beats.choice_prompt: How does Maddie challenge Lucien's takeover pitch in front of the staff?
branch_outcomes: Flirtatious mockery makes Lucien play along, sharpening their charged rivalry while entertaining Rex and worrying Dottie.
A blunt defense of local television rallies Rex and needles Blaine, turning the room's private unease into open sides-taking.
A faux-sincere business question baits Lucien into speaking more plainly, earning Dottie's cautious respect and Lucien's wary interest.
beats.exit_state: Lucien is pulled out of sterile executive mode and into a live sparring match on Maddie's terms.

beats.purpose: Transform Maddie's sniping into genuine alarm by revealing the occult undertone in Lucien's language.
beats.summary: Lucien answers with glossy executive phrasing about consolidating identities, binding independent signals into a stronger whole, and inviting superior stewardship into weakened structures. To everyone else it sounds like venomous MBA jargon, but Maddie hears the rhythm and logic of invocation language and suddenly takes him much more seriously.
beats.revelation: Lucien's merger vocabulary closely mirrors occult phrasing about binding, surrender, and inhabitation.
beats.player_goal: Listen past Lucien's polish and figure out why his words feel wrong in a way ordinary corporate slime should not.
beats.exit_state: Maddie's assessment of Lucien shifts from smug buyer to possible supernatural threat.

beats.purpose: End the scene on a sharpened threat and set Maddie's investigative intent going into the next confrontation.
beats.summary: Dottie cuts the exchange short and orders everyone back to work before the newsroom fully combusts, but the room has changed. Lucien leaves Maddie with a pointed promise that he looks forward to discussing her 'brand' in greater detail, and Maddie resolves to dig into Acheron instead of merely insulting its representative.
beats.revelation: Lucien sees Maddie and her show as a specific obstacle to neutralize or convert, not just background programming.
beats.player_goal: Leave the encounter with clarity, avoid ceding emotional ground, and commit to a next move.
beats.exit_state: Lucien gains public footing with the staff, but Maddie privately commits to investigating him as something more dangerous than a corporate raider.

color_scheme.reasoning: The palette mixes horror-host glamour with early-1990s broadcast grit: deep crimson for the campy supernatural core, warm bone and parchment tones for readable text, and a smoky muted rose-gray range for inactive UI states. Hover and selected colors are brighter and more theatrical to fit the showbiz/comedy tone, while the overall contrast stays high enough for legibility against dark, studio-like backgrounds.
